```{r setup}
library(transmap)
data(transmap_example)
```

This vignette documents the standard input data formats of `transmap`. All
functions take in-memory matrices. Reading files, quality control, covariate
selection and chromosome-specific filtering are left to the calling pipeline.

# 1. Expression matrix

All program constructors take an expression matrix `Y`:

- `Y` is an $N \times G$ numeric matrix with $N$ samples in rows and $G$ genes
  in columns.
- Sample row names and gene column names are required. Genes are matched to
  modules, programs and z-scores by name.
- Genes with zero variance must be removed before `r_hotspot()`;
  `transmap_local()` drops them automatically.

```{r expression}
Y <- transmap_example$Y
dim(Y)
Y[1:3, 1:5]
```

The expression matrix can be bulk expression, pseudo-bulk expression of one
cell type, or any other molecular phenotype measured across the same samples
(for example, protein or metabolite abundances).

# 2. Covariates

`transmap_local()` and `transmap_global()` accept an optional covariate matrix:

- `covariates` is a numeric matrix with sample row names (for example, genotype
  principal components, sex, age and batch).
- Samples are matched to `Y` by row name and only shared samples are kept.
- Covariates and an intercept are regressed out of every gene before programs
  are built.

```{r covariates}
head(transmap_example$covariates, 3)
```

`r_hotspot()` does not take covariates; regress them out of `Y` before module
detection if needed.

# 3. Gene modules (TransMap-local)

`transmap_local()` accepts gene modules in three forms:

- the result of `r_hotspot()`;
- a named list of character vectors, one per module;
- a single character vector of genes (treated as one module).

```{r modules}
str(transmap_example$modules)
```

Genes that are not in `Y` are ignored.

# 4. Null trans z-scores (WPC)

The default local constructor, whitened principal components (WPC), needs
null *trans* z-scores to estimate the gene-gene correlation expected without
genetic effects:

- `null_z` is a numeric matrix with variants in rows and genes in columns
  (gene column names required), or a list with element `z` holding that matrix.
- It must contain every module gene present in `Y`.
- Only variants whose largest absolute z-score across the module genes is below
  2 (relaxed to 3 if too few remain) are used.

```{r null-z}
dim(transmap_example$null_z)
transmap_example$null_z[1:3, 1:4]
```

In practice, `null_z` holds marginal *trans* z-scores of a large set of
variants, most of which have no effect on the module genes.

# 5. Association statistics (TransMap-global)

`r_transcca()` and `w_construction()` take a named list `data_list` of
variant-gene association statistics, in the format of transBoost's `data.list`.
Variants are in rows and genes in columns; matrices need row and column names.
The list holds exactly one of the following sets of elements:

| `data_list` elements | Description | $W$ used by transCCA |
|---|---|---|
| `Z`, `N` | Marginal z-scores and sample size | $Z / \sqrt{N - 2 + Z^2}$ |
| `Beta` | Standardized effect sizes | `Beta` |
| `Beta`, `N` + one of `Pvalue`, `Z`, `seBeta` | Unstandardized effect sizes | `Beta` rescaled by an estimated genotype scale |
| `log2FC`, `N1`, `N0` | Differential expression between two groups | $\sqrt{N_1 N_0} / (N_1 + N_0) \cdot \log_2 FC$ |
| `G`, `E` | Individual-level genotypes and expression | $G^\top E / N$ |
| `Sigma_GE` | A precomputed variant-gene matrix | `Sigma_GE` |

Optional elements:

- `MAF` (one value per variant) and `sdY` (one value per gene) rescale `Z, N`
  or `Beta` input to the effect scale.
- `Sigma_GG` (variant correlation) and/or `Sigma_EE` (gene correlation) whiten
  $W$ as $\Sigma_{GG}^{-1/2} W \Sigma_{EE}^{-1/2}$. With `G` and `E`,
  `"insample"` uses the sample covariance.

The simplest input is a z-score matrix with its sample size:

```{r data-list}
data_list <- list(Z = transmap_example$z, N = transmap_example$n)
dim(data_list$Z)
data_list$Z[1:3, 1:4]
```

See [Constructing the W Matrix](Constructing_W_Matrix.html) for an example of
every input type, whitening and *cis* masking.

# 6. Example data

`transmap_example` is a small simulated data set used throughout the
tutorials:

- `Y`: 300 samples $\times$ 60 genes. Genes `GENE01`-`GENE12`,
  `GENE13`-`GENE24` and `GENE25`-`GENE36` form three co-expression modules;
  the other genes are noise.
- `covariates`: 300 $\times$ 2 covariate matrix.
- `modules`: the three simulated modules.
- `null_z`: 400 variants $\times$ 60 genes of null *trans* z-scores.
- `z`: 150 variants $\times$ 60 genes of marginal *trans* z-scores with two
  global programs: variants 1-10 affect `GENE01`-`GENE12`, and variants 11-20
  affect `GENE25`-`GENE36` and `GENE40`-`GENE45`.
- `n`: the sample size of `z`.

The script that generates the data is `data-raw/transmap_example.R` in the
package source.
